newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank fails to inject funds.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank fails to inject funds.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank said it did not inject funds into the banking system through open market operations on Wednesday as planned due to a lack of demand from financial institutions.
The bank had said it would execute open market operations through bills finance companies, using qualified securities instruments offered by interested financial institutions.
The qualified instruments were limited to central bank negotiable certificates of deposit. The specified term was within-one-day.
The bank on Tuesday injected T$38.37 billion worth of funds into the banking system through open market operations, something it had not done since late February.
Dealers noted that a tight liquidity situation has eased.
At 0400 GMT, the overnight interbank rate had dipped to 6.241 percent, well above the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone but below Tuesday's 6.489 close.
Thirty-day commercial paper down to 5.65-5.75 compared to 6.00-6.25 on Tuesday.
